96. Any notice required to be given under these articles of association shall be in writing.
97. The Investment Club may give any notice to a member either personally or by sending it by post in a prepaid envelope addressed to the member at his registered address or by leaving it at that address. In the case of joint holders of a share, all notices shall be given to the joint holder whose name stands first in the register of members in respect of the joint holding and notice so given shall be sufficient notice to all the joint holders.
98. A person present, either in person or by proxy, at any meeting shall be deemed to have received notice of the meeting.
99. Every person who becomes entitled to a share shall be bound by any notice in respect of that share.
100. Proof that an envelope containing a notice was properly addressed, prepaid and posted is conclusive evidence that the notice was given 48 hours after it was posted. A notice shall be deemed to be given at the expiration of 48 hours after the envelope containing it was posted.
101. A notice may be given by the Investment Club to the persons entitled to a share in consequence of the death or bankruptcy of a member by sending or delivering it, at the address, supplied for that purpose by the persons claiming to be so entitled. Until such an address has been supplied, a notice may be given in any manner in which it might have been given if the death or bankruptcy had not occurred.

102. An Investment Club and each Member are taken to indemnify each director of the Investment Club in respect of any liability incurred or sustained by him or her (including any actual liability, costs or expenses reasonable incurred or sustained) in connection with any debt claim, action or obligation of any kind in which he or she becomes involved by virtue of being a director, unless the claim, action, or obligation arises as a result of fraud, gross negligence or wilful default on the part of the director.
103. Each Member is taken to indemnify each other Member in respect of any liability incurred or sustained by the other Member (including any actual liability, costs or expenses reasonable incurred or sustained) in connection with any claim or action by a Member against another Member, unless the claim or action arises as a result of fraud, gross negligence or wilful default on the part of the Member the subject of the claim or action.

QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.title: LLP 1.3.1
QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.document_html:
In these rules:

(A) defined terms are identified by the capitalisation of the initial letter of the word or phrase and are in italics;
(B) subject to (C) defined terms have the same meaning as they have in the Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations; and
(C) the following defined terms have the meaning given below:

Defined Term Meaning
Authorisation Authorisation granted by the Regulatory Authority to carry on Regulated Activities in accordance with Part 5 of the Financial Services Regulations.
CRO Companies Registration Office
Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations The QFC Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations 2005
Islamic Financial Business The business of carrying on one or more Regulated Activities in accordance with Shari'a.
Person Any person and includes a natural or legal person, body corporate, or body unincorporate, including a branch, company, Partnerships, unincorporated association or other undertaking, government or state.
Regulated Activities Has the meaning set out in Article 23 of the Financial Services Regulations.

Inserted by from RM2011-2 (as from 6th December 2011).

QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.document_html:
Any form, annexure or other document filed with the CRO must:

(A) be on white paper of international A4 size;
(B) be clearly printed or written in black in a manner that is permanent and is able to be reproduced or copied by photographic or electronic means;
(C) contain, where applicable, original signatures of the person or persons indicated on the form and the date on which they signed;
(D) set out the name and QFC number (where applicable) of the Limited Liability Partnerships or Branch to which the form relates; and
(E) be completed in the English language.
Inserted by from RM2011-2 (as from 6th December 2011).

doc_path: LLP 2 Limited Liability Partnerships registry, Forms and Fees
QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.document_html:
Where a provision of the Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations or these rules requires a certified copy of a document to be filed with the CRO, the copy must be certified by:

(A) in the case of a document created or issued by a Limited Liability Partnerships or Non-QFC Limited Liability Partnerships itself, including but not limited to the Limited Liability Partnerships Agreement and other constitutional documents, a Member or Designated Member of the Limited Liability Partnerships or Non-QFC Limited Liability Partnerships;
(B) in the case of a document issued by the public body responsible for the incorporation of companies or the maintenance of the company registry in another jurisdiction, a person properly authorised by that public body; or
(C) in any other case, a person duly authorised to certify official documents in the jurisdiction in which the copy is being certified.
Inserted by from RM2011-2 (as from 6th December 2011).

QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.title: LLP 4.2.1
doc_path: LLP 4.2 Objection to Notice of Financial Penalty
QFCA Rules :: Limited Liability Partners.document_html:
To object to the imposition of a financial penalty in accordance with Article 57(3)(B) of the Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations, a person must file with the CRO within the period stated in the notice of imposition of financial penalty a notice of objection which sets out the following information:

(A) the name of the person to whom the notice of imposition of financial penalty was addressed;
(B) the date of the notice of imposition of financial penalty;
(C) the period within which objection to the imposition of financial penalty must be made; and
(D) every matter which the person believes ought to be taken into account by the CRO in determining whether to commence proceedings in the Regulatory Tribunal for payment of financial penalty.
Inserted by from RM2011-2 (as from 6th December 2011).

doc_path: NRA Part One - Application, Interpretation, and Definitions
QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
The purpose of these rules is to provide further detail in respect of the Non-Regulated Activities for which an Entity may be licensed by the QFCA and to provide in particular for: 

(A) the categories of Non-Regulated Activities which may be carried on by a Licensed Firm; and
(B) the conditions and restrictions applicable to Non-Regulated Activities.

1.3.1 In these rules:
(A) a reference to a provision of a law, regulation or rule includes a reference to that provision as amended or re-enacted from time to time;
(B) year means a year of the Gregorian calendar;
(C) month means a month of the Gregorian calendar;
(D) a reference to the masculine gender includes the feminine and the neuter;
(E) a reference to writing includes any form of representing or reproducing words in legible form; and
(F) headings do not affect interpretation.
1.3.2 A reference in a provision of these rules to a paragraph, sub-paragraph or rule by number or letter only, without further identification, is a reference to the paragraph, sub-paragraph or rule of that number or letter contained in the provision of these rules in which that reference occurs.
1.3.3 In these rules, "include", "including", "in particular", "for example", "such as" or similar expressions are not to be construed as limiting the generality of the words preceding them.

QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.title: NRA 1.4 Definitions
doc_path: NRA Part One - Application, Interpretation, and Definitions
QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
“Authorised Firm” means a body corporate, partnership or unincorporated association which has been granted and continues to hold an authorisation granted by the QFCRA to conduct a Regulated Activity.

“Entity” means a body corporate or partnership or unincorporated association carrying on business with a view to a profit.

“Group” means, with respect to an Entity:

(A) any parent Entity of the Entity;
(B) any subsidiary (direct or indirect) of that Entity or of any parent Entity of that Entity; and
(C) that Entity.

“Licence” a licence, approval or authorisation to operate in the QFC issued by the QFCA pursuant to Article 11.1 of the QFC Law.

“Licensed Firm” means a body corporate, partnership or unincorporated association which has been granted and continues to hold a Licence granted by the QFCA.

“LLC(G)” a company established pursuant to Part 3A of the Companies Regulations 2005.

“Non-Regulated Activities” means, in addition to Structure-Based Activities, the activities listed in these rules.

“Person” includes a natural or legal person, body corporate, or body unincorporate, including a branch, company, partnership, unincorporated association or other undertaking, government or State.

“QFC” means the Qatar Financial Centre.

“QFC Entity” means a Person licensed or registered in the QFC, including a Licensed Firm and an Authorised Firm.

“QFC Law” means Law No. (7) of Year 2005 as amended.

“QFCA” means the Qatar Financial Centre Authority.

“QFCRA” means the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority.

“Regulated Activity” has the meaning set out in Article 23 of the QFC Financial Services Regulations.

“Senior Executive Function” has the meaning set out in General Rule 11.3 of the QFCA Rules. 

“State” means the State of Qatar.

“Structure-Based Activities” means the activities listed in the Foundation Regulations 2016, the Investment Clubs Regulations 2016, the Single Family Office Regulations, and the Special Company Regulations.

QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.title: NRA Part Two – Classification of Non-Regulated Activities
doc_path: NRA Part Two – Classification of Non-Regulated Activities
QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
2.1 Other than Structure-Based Activities, all activities licensed by theQFCA are categorised into 1 or more activity clusters. A cluster may be divided into subclusters.
2.2 Each cluster or subcluster is made up of 1 or more business activities. Each business activity is assigned a unique code.
2.3 The clusters, the subclusters (if any) of each cluster, and the activities within each cluster or subcluster and their codes, and any special conditions and/or restrictions applicable to engaging in a business activity, are set out in Part Four of these rules.

2.4 In Part Four:

(A) an activity cluster is identified by an alphanumeric code beginning with “C” followed by 1 or 2 digits (for example “C10 – Advisory and Consultancy”) and a title;
(B) an activity subcluster is identified by the same alphanumeric code of its parent cluster followed by a decimal point and 1 or 2 digits (for example “C10.1 – Management and Business Consultancy”) and a title; and
(C) a business activity is identified with a numeric symbol consisting of 4 digits followed by a dash and 3 further digits, and is described.

QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.title: NRA Part Three — Licensing
QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
3.1 ALicensed Firm may carry on aNon-Regulated Activity only if itslicence permits it to do so, subject to any such conditions, restrictions or requirements as theQFCA considers appropriate. If any such conditions, restrictions or requirements conflict with a Non-Regulated Activity, that condition, restriction or requirement prevails.
3.2 ALicence may be granted to carry on one or more activities from the clusters outlined in these rules. TheLicence must specify the specificNon-Regulated Activities that theLicensed Firm is permitted to carry on and the clusters (or subclusters, if applicable) within which thoseNon-Regulated Activities fall.

3.3 ALicensed Firm may not carry on any of the following activities:

(A) manpower supply and outsourcing, unless licensed to conduct “C33 -Temporary Employment Agency Activities”;
(B) arranging sponsorship and visas, unless licensed;
(C) the supply of goods or hardware by way of business;
(D) any activity that typically or primarily involves manual labour;
(E) any activity that is classified as charitable by any law of the State;
(F) anyRegulated Activity unless it has an appropriate approval, authorisation orlicence from the QFCRA; or
(G) act as a real estate agent or real estate broker.
3.4 ALicensed Firm may recruit only the appropriate number of manual labourers and support staff as is reasonably required to carry on the activities set out in its License.
3.5 ALicensed Firm is a “Designated Non-Financial Business or Profession” if it meets the criteria outlined in the “Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Rules 2019”.
3.6 Nothing in these rules restricts the power of the QFCA, as set out in any other rules or regulation, to impose any conditions or restrictions on theLicence of a Licensed Firm.
3.7 ALicensed Firm is expected to possess the required knowledge and skill for carrying on the activities set out in its Licence.
3.8 If aLicensed Firm is required under these rules to obtain professional indemnity insurance, such insurance must be adequate to the operations and risks of the activities of such Licensed Firm.

QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
4.3.1 The activity cluster “C5 — Group Holding and Management Office” includes the following business activities:

(A) 7011-001 – Holding controlling levels of equity in the assets of a Group of subsidiary corporations with the principal activity of owning its Group and providing associated ancillary services;
(B) 7011-002 – Granting any type of security interest for its own benefit or for the benefit of any entity within its own Group;
(C) 7011-003 – Providing an indemnity, guarantee or similar support to any third party for its own benefit or for the benefit of any entity within its own Group;
(D) 7011-004 – Acquiring, holding or disposing of any interest in any asset for its own benefit or for the benefit of any entity within its own Group;
(E) 7011-005 – Providing any type of loan or other form of financing to any entity within its own Group;
(F) 7011-006 - Managing the operations of other members of its Group; and
(G) 7011-007 – Additional ancillary activities in relation to providing security interests, indemnities or guarantees.

4.3.2 Unless otherwise permitted by the QFCA, a Licensed Firm that is a Group Holding and Management Office may not provide its services to any Person outside its Group.

QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.title: NRA C13A - Token Services
doc_path: NRA Part Four – Classification of Non-Regulated Activities
QFCA Rules :: Non-Regulated Activities R.document_html:
4.4.32B The activity cluster “C13A – Token Services” includes the following business activities unless they constitute a regulated activity by virtue of the Investment Token Rules 2024:

(A) 6213-001 – validation: the services of:

(i) confirming that a person is the owner of a right capable of being represented by a permitted token; and
(ii) issuing a certificate of validation;
(B) 6213-002 – token generation: the service of generating a token on token infrastructure on behalf of the owner of the underlying represented by the token;

(C) 6213-003 – token custody services: the service of:

(i) holding or controlling tokens on behalf of clients; and
(ii) holding or controlling the means by which clients’ tokens may be recorded and transacted on token infrastructure;
(D) 6213-004 – operating a token exchange: operating a system which brings together multiple third party buying and selling interests in tokens, in accordance with the system’s non-discretionary rules, in a way that results in a contract in respect of the tokens. This excludes an entity which operates a facility which is merely an order routing system where buying and selling interests in, or orders for, tokens are merely transmitted but do not interact; and
(E) 6213-005 – token transfer services: providing any service (other than validation, token generation, token custody services or operating a token exchange) that facilitates the transfer of a token to, or from, a person from, or to, a third party. This excludes the selling of hardware or software which may be used in relation to the transfer of a token.
4.4.32C Unless otherwise permitted by the QFCA, aLicensed Firm that provides Token Services must obtain professional indemnity insurance.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 1. Application
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
The rules set out herein shall be referred to as the QFCA Rules. These QFCA Rules are made pursuant to Article 12 of the QFC Authority Regulations.

The QFCA Rules shall apply to all Licensed Firms and where specified in Table 1 below to Authorised Firms in respect of a Relevant Requirement. The QFCA Rules also apply to Applicants, as relevant, and references to Licensed or Authorised Firms shall include, where the context requires, Applicants to become Licensed or Authorised Firms. If the context requires, these rules also apply to a Person.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 2. Interpretation
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
In the QFCA Rules, a reference to:

(A) a provision of any law, regulation or rule includes a reference to that provision as amended or re-enacted from time to time;
(B) a calendar year shall mean a year of the Gregorian calendar;
(C) a month shall mean a month of the Gregorian calendar;
(D) the masculine gender includes the feminine and the neuter;
(E) writing includes any form of representing or reproducing words in legible form; and
(F) a Person is, where the context permits, to any Person in respect of which the QFCA has jurisdiction under or pursuant to the QFC Law or Regulations or Rules or whose conduct or activities are or may be subject to the QFC Law, Regulations or Rules.

The headings in the QFCA Rules shall not affect its interpretation.

A reference in a rule or other part or Schedule of the QFCA Rules to a paragraph, sub-paragraph or rule by number or letter only, and without further identification, is a reference to a paragraph, sub-paragraph or rule of that number or letter contained in the rule or other part or Schedule of the QFCA Rules in which that reference occurs.

Each of the Schedules to the QFCA Rules shall have effect as if set out in the QFCA Rules and reference to QFCA Rules shall include reference to the Schedule.

Any reference in QFCA Rules to "include", "including", "in particular", "for example", "such as" or similar expressions shall be considered as being by way of illustration or emphasis only and are not to be construed so as to limit the generality of any words preceding them.

Footnotes in QFCA Rules are not binding.

Amended (as from 19th October 2017)
Amended (as from June 2022)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 3. Definitions
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
"Accountancy" refers to the corresponding subcluster of business activities that anentity may be licensed or registered to carry on in accordance with the Non-Regulated Activities Rules.

"Accreditation" refers to the corresponding cluster of business activities that anentity may be licensed or registered to carry on in accordance with the Non-Regulated Activities Rules.

"Activities of LLC(G)s" refers to the corresponding cluster of business activities that anentity may be licensed to carry on in accordance with the Non-Regulated Activities Rules.

"AML/CFT Law" means Law No. (20) of 2019 onCombating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing.

"AML/CFT Rules" means theAnti-Money Laundering andCombating Terrorist Financing Rules 2010 of theQFC Regulatory Authority as amended from time to time.

"Applicant" means a Person submitting an Application.

"Application" means an application:

(A) for aQFCA Licence or variation or withdrawal of aQFCA Licence or QFC Regulatory Authority Authorisation;
(B) for an approval of aPerson to undertake a specified function, including the appointment of aPerson as aKey Person or Interest Holder; or
(C) for Guidance or a waiver (or revocation or variation of a waiver) of Rules as the context requires.

"Authorised Firm" means a person authorised by theQFC Regulatory Authority to engage in Regulated Activities as set forth in Article 23 of QFC Financial Services Regulations.

"Business Day" means any day which is not a Friday, a Saturday or a public holiday in the State of Qatar.

"CER Rules" means the Compliance and Enforcement Rules set out inPart 5 of these QFCA Rules.

"Client" means any person who enters into a transaction with aLicensed Firm in respect of a Non-Regulated Activity, including the receipt of advice and any other business or service undertaken by aLicensed Firm in the course of carrying out aNon-Regulated Activity in or from the QFC.

"Client Money" means all money held or received by a Licensed Firm:

(A) from or on behalf of aClient in the course of or in connection with the carrying on of aNon-Regulated Activity in or from the QFC; or
(B) which aLicensed Firm treats asClient Money in accordance with LFAR.

"COB Rules" means the conduct of business rules set out inPart 3 of these QFCA Rules.

"CRO" means the Companies Registration Office established pursuant to Article 7 of the QFC Law.

"Eligible Bank" means aPerson that is anAuthorised Firm with an authorisation for deposit taking, or a person in relation to whom all of the following requirements are satisfied:

(A) thePerson is incorporated in a jurisdiction outside the QFC;
(B) theRegulatory Authority has not, by notice, declared that this definition does not apply to the jurisdiction;
(C) thePerson is regulated as a bank, and principally regulated for prudential purposes, by an overseas regulator in the jurisdiction;
(D) thePerson is required to prepare audited accounts;
(E) thePerson has minimum assets of US $10 million (or its equivalent in any other currency at the relevant time);
(F) thePerson had surplus revenue over expenditure for thePerson's last 2 financial years; and
(G) thePerson's latest annual audit report is not materially qualified.

"Entity" means abody corporate or partnership or unincorporated association carrying on business with a view to a profit.

"Financial Services Regulations" means the QFC Financial Services Regulations No. (1) of 2005.

"Firm-Related Distribution Event" for a Licensed Firm:

(A) the appointment of a liquidator, receiver or administrator or of a trustee in bankruptcy; or
(B) an event in any jurisdiction equivalent to an appointment mentioned in paragraph (A);
(C) the withdrawal or cancellation by theQFCA of theLicensed Firms' Licence; or
(D) the imposition or variation of a condition, restriction or requirement on theLicensed Firms'Licence so that it is no longer permitted to hold Client Money.

"General Rules" means the general rules set out inPart 2 of these QFCA Rules.

"Group" means with respect to an Entity:

(A) that Entity;
(B) any parentEntity of the Entity; and
(C) any subsidiary (direct or indirect) of thatEntity or of any parentEntity of that Entity.

“Guidance” means guidance issued, or to be issued, by the QFC Authority under Article 14 of the QFC Authority Regulations.

"Legal Services" refers to the corresponding cluster of business activities that anentity may be licensed or registered to carry on in accordance with the Non-Regulated Activities Rules.

"LFAR" means Licensed Firm Asset Rules set out inPart 4 of these QFCA Rules.

"Licensed Firm" means a person licensed by theQFCA to engage in Non-Regulated Activities in or from the QFC, and that is not an Authorised Firm.

"Local Licensed Firm" means aLicensed Firm incorporated in the QFC.

"MLRO" means theLicensed Firm's money laundering reporting officer.

"Non-Local Licensed Firm" means aLicensed Firm established outside theQFC and operating through a branch in the QFC.

"Non-Regulated Permitted Activities" mean the activities listed in Part 2 of Schedule 3 of the QFC Law.

"Non-Regulated Activities” means, in addition to Structure-Based Activities, the activities listed in these rules.

"Objectives" mean the Objectives of theQFCA pursuant to Article 6 of the QFC Authority Regulations.

"QFCA" means the Qatar Financial Centre Authority.

doc_path: General Rule 2. Licence to Conduct Non-Regulated Activities
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
In order to become and remain a Licensed Firm, a Person shall ensure it is and remains fit and proper and complies with any Regulations and Rules as well as the QFCA Rules that may apply to the particular type of Non-Regulated Activities undertaken and shall conduct itself at all times in a manner that (A) reflects and promotes the spirit, purpose and Objectives of the general principles set out in Schedule 1 (the "Principles"), and (B) does not harm or hinder the QFCA in achieving its Objectives, strategies and priorities.

doc_path: General Rule 2A. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE TO THE QFC
General Rule 2A.1 TRANSFER OF REGISTRATION TO THE QFC
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
2A.1.1 A Non-QFC Company may, if authorised by the laws of the jurisdiction in which it was incorporated, apply to the CRO for the continuation of the Non-QFC Company as a QFC Entity that is not a Company (as defined in the Companies Regulations).
2A.1.2 An application for continuation must be made to the CRO using the form prescribed by the CRO and must be:
(A) executed under seal and signed by an officer or director of the Non-QFC Company and verified by an affidavit of the person signing the application;
(B) accompanied by articles of continuation that comply with the relevant provisions of the QFC regulations and rules; and
(C) accompanied by any other document prescribed by the CRO.
2A.1.3 The Non-QFC Company must make any amendments to the original articles of incorporation that are necessary to make the articles of continuation conform to the relevant provisions of the QFC’s regulations and rules.
2A.1.4 For the purpose of this Rule 2A, articles of association means the Non-QFC Company’s updated constitutional document registered in the jurisdiction from where it is migrating, and articles of continuation means the Non-QFC Company’s updated constitutional document amended as described in Rule 2A.1(3) above.
Added (as from October 2023)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 2A.2 CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUATION AND LICENCE CERTIFICATE
doc_path: General Rule 2A. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE TO THE QFC
General Rule 2A.2 CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUATION AND LICENCE CERTIFICATE
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
2A.2.1 Should the CRO approve the application, the CRO will:
(A) issue a certificate of continuation on the terms and conditions it considers appropriate;
(B) register the Non-QFC Company as a QFC Entity; and
(C) allocate to the QFC Entity a number, which shall be the QFC Entity’s registered number.
2A.2.2 On or after its registration, the QFC Authority may issue a licence to the QFC Entity, to conduct one or more Non-Regulated Activities which correspond most closely to the activities the non-QFC Company was licensed or permitted to conduct in the original jurisdiction.
2A.2.3 The CRO may refuse to issue a certificate of continuation if it considers it appropriate to do so.
2A.2.4 The CRO is not required to provide reasons for refusing to issue a certificate of continuation.
Added (as from October 2023)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 2A.3 EFFECT OF CERTIFICATE
doc_path: General Rule 2A. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE TO THE QFC
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
From the date of continuation stated in the certificate of continuation:
2A.3.1 the Non-QFC Company becomes a QFC Entity to which the QFC regulations and rules apply as if it has been incorporated or established in the QFC;
2A.3.2 the articles of continuation become the constitutional document of the QFC Entity; and
2A.3.3 the certificate of continuation is treated as the certificate of incorporation or certificate of establishment, as the case may be, of the QFC Entity.
Added (as from October 2023)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 2A.5 RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES
doc_path: General Rule 2A. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE TO THE QFC
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Where a Non-QFC Company is continued as a QFC Entity under this Rule, the QFC Entity:

2A.5.1 continues to have all the property, rights and privileges and is subject to all the liabilities, disabilities and debts that it had before the continuation; and
2A.5.2 remains a party in any legal proceedings commenced in any jurisdiction in which it was a party before the continuation.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 2A.6 APPLICATION
doc_path: General Rule 2A. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE TO THE QFC
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
2A.6.1 An application pursuant to this Rule 2A must be accompanied by:
(A) the articles of continuation as required in Rule 2A.1(3), together with:
(i) a certified copy of the Non-QFC Company’s current certificate of incorporation or document of similar effect and any amendments thereto; and
(ii) a certified copy of the Non-QFC Company’s articles of association or other constitutional document of similar effect and any amendments thereto;
(B) evidence satisfactory to the CRO that the Non-QFC Company is permitted by the laws of the jurisdiction in which it is incorporated to be continued under the laws of another jurisdiction and that it has complied with all the relevant requirements;
(C) evidence satisfactory to the CRO that all necessary consents in the original jurisdiction of incorporation, including but not limited to any necessary consent of shareholders or its equivalents, have been obtained and certified;
(D) a copy of the Non-QFC Company’s most recent audited accounts filed with the relevant authority in the jurisdiction in which it is incorporated or otherwise to the satisfaction of the CRO; and
(E) the relevant prescribed fee prescribed in Schedule 4.
(F) If any documents submitted to the CRO are not in the English language, the documents must be accompanied by a certified English translation.
(G) A Non-QFC Company must not apply to the CRO under this Rule 2A, unless the directors or members of its governing body have filed with the CRO a declaration that:
(1) the Non-QFC Company is solvent;
(2) at the time of the application, there is no reasonable prospect of the Non-QFC Company becoming insolvent; and
(3) there are no applications made to any court:
(a) to put the Non-QFC Company into liquidation;
(b) to wind up the Non-QFC Company;
(c) to have the Non-QFC Company declared insolvent; or
(d) for the appointment of a receiver in relation to any property of the Non-QFC Company.
2A.6.2 A Non-QFC Company which conducts an activity that is a regulated activity under the Financial Services Regulations and wishes to transfer its incorporation to the QFC and be continued as a QFC Entity under this Rule 2A must obtain the prior written consent of the Regulatory Authority.
2A.6.3 A certificate of continuation is conclusive evidence that the Non-QFC Company is a duly registered QFC Entity from the date of continuation stated in the certificate.
2A.6.4 Where a Non-QFC Company is continued as a QFC Entity, the QFC Entity must file with the CRO any certificate or document issued under the laws of the jurisdiction of the Non-QFC Company evidencing the fact the Non-QFC Company has ceased to be incorporated under the laws of that jurisdiction.
Added (as from October 2023)

General Rule 2B.1 TRANSFER OF REGISTRATION FROM THE QFC TO ANOTHER JURISDICTION
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
2B.1.1 A Licensed Firm that is not a Company (as defined in the Companies Regulations) may, if it is authorised by:
(A) a decision of its governing body approved by not less than two third of its members; and
(B) the CRO,
apply to the appropriate official or public body of a foreign jurisdiction to transfer its incorporation to the foreign jurisdiction and request that the Licensed Firm be continued as a Non-QFC Company.
2B.1.2 A Licenced Firm may not apply under this Rule 2B unless the laws of the foreign jurisdiction provide that the Licenced Firm will:
(A) continue to have all the property, rights and privileges and is subject to all the liabilities, disabilities and debts that it had before the continuation; and
(B) remain a party in any legal proceedings commenced in any jurisdiction in which it was a party before the continuation.
2B.1.3 A Licensed Firm ceases to be a QFC Entity when the QFC Entity is continued as a Non-QFC Company and when it files with the CRO a copy of the certificate or instrument of continuation certified by the appropriate official of the foreign jurisdiction.
2B.1.4 When the CRO receives the foreign jurisdiction’s certificate or instrument of continuation, the CRO must strike the name of the Licensed Firm off the index of names maintained by the CRO.
2B.1.5 The CRO may refuse to authorise a Licensed Firm to apply to transfer its incorporation to a foreign jurisdiction and be continued as a Non-QFC Company under this Rule 2B.
Added (as from October 2023)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 2B.2 APPLICATION
doc_path: General Rule 2B. MIGRATION OF BODY CORPORATE FROM THE QFC
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
2B.2.1 A Licensed Firm, must apply in writing to the CRO and such application must be accompanied by:
(A) a certified copy of the decision of its governing body approving that the Licensed Firm may transfer its incorporation to a foreign jurisdiction and be continued as a Non-QFC Company;
(B) evidence acceptable to the CRO that:
(i) the Licensed Firm is able to transfer its incorporation and be continued under the laws of the other jurisdiction; and
(ii) the laws of the other jurisdiction satisfy the requirements set out in this Rule 2B;
(C) the Regulatory Authority’s written consent if the Licensed Firm is a designated non-financial business or profession (within the meaning of the AML/CFT Rules);
(D) any declaration, certification, information, document or confirmation as the CRO may require; and the relevant fee prescribed in Schedule 4.
2B.2.2 A Licensed Firm must not apply to the CRO under Rule 2B unless the members of its governing body have filed with the CRO a declaration that:
(A) the Licensed Firm is solvent;
(B) at the time of the application, there is no reasonable prospect of the Licensed Firm becoming insolvent; and
(C) there are no applications made to any court:
i. to put the Licensed Firm into liquidation;
ii. to wind up the Licensed Firm;
iii. to have the Licensed Firm declared insolvent; or
iv. for the appointment of a receiver in relation to any property of the Licensed Firm.
2B.2.3 A Licensed Firm making an application under Rule 2B must place a legible and comprehensible notice 60 days prior to making such an application in one or more newspapers or other publication best suited to bring the proposed transfer of incorporation to the attention of any persons who may be affected by such transfer.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 3.2.2

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) A Licensed Firm must take reasonable care to ensure that all business documents in connection with the carrying on of Non-Regulated Activities in or from the QFC include one of the disclosures in General Rule 3.2.2(C).
(B) The expression "business documents":
(i) includes, but is not limited to, letterheads, whether issued by post, fax or electronic means, terms of business, Client agreements, written financial communications, business cards, prospectuses and websites; but
(ii) does not include compliment slips, account statements or text messages.
(C) The disclosure required under this General Rule is:
(i) "Licensed by the Qatar Financial Centre Authority"; or
(ii) "Licensed by the QFCA".
(D) The QFCA logo must only be reproduced with the express written permission of the QFCA and in accordance with any conditions for use issued from time to time.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 3.3.1
doc_path: General Rule 3.3 Communication with the QFCA and the CRO
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Without prejudice to any other provision of these Rules all communications made by a Licensed or Authorised Firm to the QFCA or the CRO whether pursuant to any Regulations, Rules, or otherwise shall be made by an employee (officer or otherwise) of the Licensed or Authorised Firm authorised to make such communication to the QFCA or the CRO and shall be in English unless otherwise permitted by the QFCA or the CRO.

All internal procedures, records or other documentation created by the Licensed or Authorised Firm shall be in English.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 3.3.2
doc_path: General Rule 3.3 Communication with the QFCA and the CRO
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) The QFCA may operate an electronic submission system (Electronic System) to allow Licensed Firms, Authorised Firms, or other Persons approved in writing by the QFCA (Registered Users) to communicate with it or with the CRO, to produce documents and information in an electronic form. The QFCA may issue instructions for, amongst other things:
(i) access to, guidelines concerning and the use of the Electronic System;
(ii) QFCA's approval of any individuals nominated to access and use the Electronic System on behalf of a Registered User;
(iii) withdrawal of access to Registered Users or any individual previously approved to access and use the Electronic System on behalf a Registered User; and
(iv) measures that the QFCA considers necessary or desirable to maintain the integrity and security of the Electronic System.
(B) The Registered User must ensure that:
(i) only suitable individuals have access to the Electronic System;
(ii) individuals who have access to the Electronic System follow the usage instructions and use the Electronic System properly;
(iii) it has adequate policies, procedures, systems and controls to comply with this Rule 3.3; and keep necessary records; and
(iv) it and its directors, officers, employees, agents and contractors do not do, or fail to do, anything that compromises the integrity or security of the Electronic System.
(C) If a communication is made to the QFCA or the CRO using the Electronic System, the communication will be deemed to have been made at the time it is received by the QFCA or the CRO; and for the purposes of these Rules, to have been Signed and made in writing.
(D) This rule is additional to, and does not limit, the generality of Rule 3.3.1 (Communication with the QFCA and the CRO), any other provision of these Rules or any other Rules.
Amended (as from 23rd September 2014)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 4.5.1
doc_path: General Rule 4. Notices to the QFCA
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A Licensed Firm must notify the QFCA immediately if one of the following events arises in relation to its activities in or from the QFC:

(A) it becomes aware that an employee may have committed a fraud against one of its Client;
(B) a serious fraud has been committed against it;
(C) it has reason to believe that a Person is acting with intent to commit a serious fraud against it; or
(D) it identifies significant irregularities in its accounting or other records, whether or not there is evidence of fraud.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) Unless a QFCA Rule states otherwise, a Licensed or Authorised Firm must ensure that each report it provides to the QFCA:
(i) contains the Licensed or Authorised Firm's name, the related QFC number and any other information required by the QFCA; and
(ii) subject to (B) is received by the QFCA during Ordinary Business Hours on the date the report is due.
(B) If the due date is not a Business Day, the report must be received by the QFCA during Ordinary Business Hours of the next Business Day.
(C) A report will not be considered to have been received by the QFCA until it has been:
(i) received by the QFCA; and
(ii) duly Signed by the signatories specified in the relevant QFCA Rule and delivered:
(1) by email or Electronic System;
(2) by post to the current address of the QFCA;
(3) hand delivered to the current address of the QFCA; or
(4) faxed to a fax number provided by the QFCA.

(C) A report will not be considered to have been received by the QFCA until it has been: (i) received by the QFCA ; and (ii) duly Signed by the signatories specified in the relevant QFCA Rule and delivered: (1) by email or Electronic System; (2) by post to the current address of the QFCA ; (3) hand delivered to the current address of the QFCA ; or (4) faxed to a fax number provided by the QFCA . QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Subject to General Rule 3.3 the Licensed or Authorised Firm may maintain records created by third parties in any language. If those records are requested by the QFCA they must be reproduced in English within a reasonable period not exceeding three (3) Business Days of the date of the request.

doc_path: General Rule 7.2 Application to Waive or Modify Rules
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
The application for a Waiver or Modification Notice must contain:

(A) the Licensed or Authorised Firm's name and the related QFC number;
(B) the Relevant Requirement to which the application relates;
(C) a clear explanation of the waiver or modification that is being applied for and the reason why the Licensed or Authorised Firm is requesting it;
(D) details of any other requirements; for example, if there is a specific period for which the Waiver or Modification Notice is required;
(E) any reasons the Licensed or Authorised Firm may have as to why the Waiver or Modification Notice should not be published or why it should be published without disclosing the identity of the Licensed or Authorised Firm or the confidential or propriety nature of certain information; and
(F) all relevant facts to support the application.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:

(A) either:
(i) the burden experienced by that Person in complying with the Relevant Requirement would significantly outweigh the benefits that the Relevant Requirement was intended to achieve; or

(B) the notice would not result in undue risk to Persons whose interests the QFCA Rule is intended to protect.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.1 Definitions
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
In Rule 8A:

“Basic Information” means the information as determined and set out in Rule 8A.1A.

"Beneficial Owner" has the meaning set out in Rule 8A.3.

“Civil and Commercial Court” means the Civil and Commercial Court of the QFC established under Article 8 of the QFC Law.

"Foundation" means a foundation established under the Foundation Regulations.

"Governing Body" means

(a) for a company or a company limited by guarantee, its board of directors;
(b) for a limited partnership, its general partner;
(c) for a trust, its trustee or trustees;
(d) for a foundation, its council; and
(e) for any other entity, its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body.

“Nominator” means one or more Person that issues directions, instructions or wishes (directly or indirectly) to a nominee to act on their behalf in the capacity of a director or a shareholder.

"Nominee Director" means a Person that acts as a director on behalf of a Nominator or in accordance with the directions, instructions or wishes of a Nominator.

"Nominee Particulars" has the meaning set out in Rule 8A.7(D).

“Nominee Shareholder” means a Person registered as a shareholder:

(a) on behalf of a Nominator or
(b) acting on the directions, instructions or wishes of a Nominator.

"QFC Entity" means a Person licensed or registered in the QFC, including a Licensed Firm and an Authorised Firm.

“Register of Basic Information” means the register of Basic Information established pursuant to Rule 8A.4.

"Register of Beneficial Owners" means the register of Beneficial Owners established pursuant to Rule 8A.4.

“Register of Nominees” means the register of nominees established pursuant to Rule 8A.7(C).

“Required Information” has the meaning set out in Rule 8A.6.

"Trust" has the meaning set out in the Trust Regulations 2007.

“Trustee” has the meaning set out in the Trust Regulations 2007.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.3 Definition of Beneficial Owner
doc_path: General Rule 8A.3 Definition of Beneficial Owner
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) A Beneficial Owner is a natural person who ultimately exercises control over a QFC Entity. The Beneficial Owner is:
(i) in relation to a company, any Person that:
(a) holds or controls, or is entitled to hold or control, directly or indirectly, or by any other means, including acting in concert with one or more Persons, 20% or more of the company’s shares;
(b) holds or controls, or is entitled to hold or control, directly or indirectly, or by any other means, including acting in concert with one or more Persons, 20% or more of the voting rights in the company;
(c) holds or controls, or is entitled to hold or control, directly or indirectly, including through contractual arrangements or by any other means, including acting in concert with one or more Persons, the right to appoint or remove a majority of the board of directors of the company; or
(d) has the right to exercise, or exercises by any means, control over the management of the company.
(ii) in relation to a company limited by guarantee, any Person that exercises by any means, or has the legal right to exercise, control or influence over the management of the company limited by guarantee, including the chief executive officer or each director.
(iii) in relation to a partnership, any Person that:
(a) holds or controls, directly or indirectly, including through contractual arrangements, or by any other means, 20% or more of the capital, profits or voting rights of that partnership; or
(b) has the right to exercise, or exercises by any means, control over the management of the partnership.
(iv) in relation to a trust:
(a) each beneficiary (or, if a specific Person is not identifiable as a beneficiary, the class of Persons for whose benefit the trust is established);
(b) the settlor of the trust or each Person performing an equivalent function;
(c) each trustee of the trust;
(d) each protector or appointer of the trust (if any); and
(e) any other Person exercising, by any means, directly or indirectly, ultimate effective control over the trust.
(v) in relation to a foundation:
(a) each beneficiary (or, if a specific Person is not identifiable as a beneficiary, the class of Persons for whose benefit the foundation is established);
(b) a founder and, if relevant, a dedicator or each Person performing equivalent function;
(c) each council member or Person performing an equivalent function; and
(d) each enforcer, protector or each Person performing an equivalent function.
(B) Where any of the roles in 8A.3(A)(i)-(v) are fulfilled by a legal person or a legal arrangement, the QFC Entity must identify the natural person who ultimately exercises control over such legal person or legal arrangement as the Beneficial Owner, unless Rule 8A.15(A) applies.
(C) A QFC Entity must trace and identify through any number of legal persons or legal arrangements of any description to reach a natural person who is the Beneficial Owner, unless Rule 8A.15(A) applies.
(D) The term “control” for the purposes of this Rule 8A includes the exercise of effective control as a result of (for example):
(i) the terms of the constitutional documents of a QFC Entity or a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of the QFC Entity;
(ii) the rights attached to the shares or securities which a Person holds, whether directly in a QFC Entity or through a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of the QFC Entity;
(iii) a shareholders or partnership agreement or other similar contractual arrangement; or
(iv) contractual or other arrangements.
(E) The right to exercise control is a right which, if exercised, would give rise to the actual exercise of control.
(F) If 2 or more natural persons jointly meet any of the criteria specified under Rule 8A.3(A)(i) – (v), each of them is taken to be a Beneficial Owner.
(G) If no natural person is identified as a Beneficial Owner of a QFC Entity, any natural person on whose instructions the QFC Entity is required or is accustomed to act or its senior managing official, is taken to be a Beneficial Owner.

(v) in relation to a foundation: (a) each beneficiary (or, if a specific Person is not identifiable as a beneficiary, the class of Persons for whose benefit the foundation is established); (b) a founder and, if relevant, a dedicator or each Person performing equivalent function; (c) each council member or Person performing an equivalent function; and (d) each enforcer, protector or each Person performing an equivalent function. (B) Where any of the roles in 8A.3(A)(i)-(v) are fulfilled by a legal person or a legal arrangement, the QFC Entity must identify the natural person who ultimately exercises control over such legal person or legal arrangement as the Beneficial Owner , unless Rule 8A.15 (A) applies. (C) A QFC Entity must trace and identify through any number of legal persons or legal arrangements of any description to reach a natural person who is the Beneficial Owner , unless Rule 8A.15 (A) applies. (D) The term “control” for the purposes of this Rule 8A includes the exercise of effective control as a result of (for example): (i) the terms of the constitutional documents of a QFC Entity or a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of the QFC Entity ; (ii) the rights attached to the shares or securities which a Person holds, whether directly in a QFC Entity or through a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of the QFC Entity ; (iii) a shareholders or partnership agreement or other similar contractual arrangement; or (iv) contractual or other arrangements. (E) The right to exercise control is a right which, if exercised, would give rise to the actual exercise of control. (F) If 2 or more natural persons jointly meet any of the criteria specified under Rule 8A.3(A)(i) – (v), each of them is taken to be a Beneficial Owner. (G) If no natural person is identified as a Beneficial Owner of a QFC Entity , any natural person on whose instructions the QFC Entity is required or is accustomed to act or its senior managing official, is taken to be a Beneficial Owner . QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.4 Obligation to Maintain a Register of Basic Information and a Register of Beneficial Owners
doc_path: General Rule 8A.4 Obligation to Maintain a Register of Basic Information and a Register of Beneficial Owners
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) In addition to the requirements of any other Regulations or Rules, a QFC Entity must establish and maintain at its registered office or principal place of business:
(i) a Register of Basic Information; and
(ii) a Register of Beneficial Owners.
(B) The Register of Basic Information and the Register of Beneficial Owners must be held and made accessible at all times during Ordinary Business Hours by:
(i) if applicable, the Senior Executive Function,
(ii) for a Foundation, the Registered Representative,
(iii) for a Single Family Office, the Designated Representative Function,
(iv) for a Branch, the Principal Representative,
(v) for a Trust, the Trustee, or
(vi) if there is no individual who performs any of the functions in Rule 8A.4(i) – (v), an individual resident in Qatar with overall responsibility for the conduct of the whole of the business of a QFC Entity.
(C) The Register of Beneficial Owners must contain the Required Information in relation to each Beneficial Owner of a QFC Entity.
(D) In relation to a Trust, the Trustee must, in addition to the information specified in Rule 8A.6(A), include in the Register of Beneficial Owners information on each of the agents and service providers to the Trust, including investment advisors or managers, accountants and tax advisors, of the following kind:
(i) for an agent or service provider that is a natural person:
(a) the information listed at 8A.6(A)(i)(a) – (e); and
(b) if different from the address provided in Rule 8A.6(A)(i)(e), the main address of the agent or service provider, that provides services to the Trust, from which it conducts its business in respect of the Trust;
(ii) for an agent or service provider that is a legal person:
(a) the information listed at 8A.6(A)(ii)(a) – (d); and
(b) if different from the address provided in Rule 8A.6(A)(ii)(d), the main address of the agent or service provider, that provides services to the Trust, from which it conducts its business in respect of the Trust,
and such information shall, in relation to such a Trust, be considered “Required Information” for the purposes of this Rule 8A.
(E) In accordance with applicable laws and regulations, each of the individuals mentioned in Rule 8A.4(B) are responsible for providing the Basic Information, the Nominee Particulars, the Required Information and any assistance required by the competent authorities when requested in a timely manner.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.6 Required Information
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) The required information is the following (the “Required Information”):
(i) for a Beneficial Owner:
(a) full name as it appears on that person's passport or other government-issued national identification document;
(b) place and date of birth;
(c) nationality (or, where that person has more than one nationality, each nationality);
(d) identifying number, country of issue, date of issue and of expiry, as set out in that person's passport or other government-issued national identification document;
(e) residential address and, if different, an address appropriate for service of notices;
(f) the date that the person became and/or ceased to be a Beneficial Owner;
(g) any percentage specified in Rule 8A.3 that is held or controlled by that person and the date of any change to such percentage;
(h) if control is exercised through means other than direct or indirect ownership of shares or control of voting rights in the relevant QFC Entity, a brief description of the basis on which such person exercises its control;
(i) the date on which the Register of Beneficial Owners was last updated; and
(j) in relation to Trusts, the information specified at Rule 8A.4(D) on agents and service providers (if any).
(ii) Without prejudice to Rules 8A.3(B) and (C), for a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of a QFC Entity, Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder and Nominator that meets any of the criteria under Rule 8A.3(A)(i)-(v):
(a) full name as it appears on that legal person’s or legal arrangement’s certificate of incorporation or establishment or similar document, or any other instrument acceptable to the CRO;
(b) the jurisdiction of incorporation, registration authority and associated registration number for the legal person or legal arrangement (or other identifying details);
(c) date of incorporation, establishment or registration;
(d) the address of record maintained with the commercial registry or similar institution with which the legal person or legal arrangement is incorporated, established or registered;
(e) the date that the legal person or legal arrangement became and/or ceased to be a legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of a QFC Entity;
(f) any percentage specified in Rule 8A.3 that is held or controlled by that legal person or legal arrangement and the date of any change to such percentage;
(g) if control is exercised through means other than direct or indirect ownership of shares or control of voting rights in the relevant QFC Entity, a brief description of the basis on which that legal person or legal arrangement exercises its control; and
(h) in relation to Trusts, the information specified at Rule 8A.4(D) on agents and service providers (if any).
(B) The QFCA or the CRO may require a QFC Entity to take one or both of the following actions:
(i) obtain, maintain and disclose, in a timely manner, Required Information about any legal person or legal arrangement in the ownership chain of a QFC Entity through which a Beneficial Owner exercises control over a QFC Entity; or
(ii) submit supporting documentation that demonstrates to the satisfaction of the QFCA or the CRO how the QFC Entity has ensured the accuracy of the Required Information.
Inserted (as from 25th June 2019)
Amended (as from 6th July 2021)
Amended (as from June 2022)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.7 Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders, Nominators and the Register of Nominees
doc_path: General Rule 8A.7 Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders, Nominators and the Register of Nominees
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) A Nominee Director or Nominee Shareholder must:
(i) inform each QFC Entity in relation to which it acts as nominee, of the fact that it is a Nominee Director or Nominee Shareholder (as the case may be); and
(ii) provide the QFC Entity with its Nominee Particulars as a Nominee Director or Nominee Shareholder (as the case may be) and the Nominee Particulars of the Nominator.
(B) The QFC Entity must identify the Beneficial Owner of each Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder and Nominator and obtain the related Required Information.
(C) A QFC Entity which has one or more Nominee Directors or Nominee Shareholders must establish, maintain and hold a Register of Nominees containing the Nominee Particulars in relation to:
(i) each Nominee Director;
(ii) each Nominee Shareholder; and
(iii) each Nominator.
(D) The Nominee Particulars are as follows:
(i) for a natural person, the information listed at 8A.6(A)(i)(a) – (e);
(ii) for legal persons or legal arrangements, the information listed at 8A.6(A)(ii)(a)-(d);
(iii) the date on which the Nominee Director became a director of the QFC Entity;
(iv) the date on which the Nominator of the Nominee Director became a Nominator;
(v) the date on which the Nominee Director ceased to be a director of the QFC Entity;
(vi) the date on which the Nominator of the Nominee Director ceased to be the Nominator;
(vii) the date on which the Nominee Shareholder became a shareholder of the QFC Entity;
(viii) the date on which the Nominator of the Nominee Shareholder became a Nominator;
(ix) the date on which the Nominee Shareholder ceased to be a shareholder of the QFC Entity;
(x) the date on which the Nominator of the Nominee Shareholder ceased to be a Nominator;
(xi) the Required Information in respect of the Beneficial Owner of each Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder and Nominator; and
(xii) the date on which the Register of Nominees was last updated.
(E) Rule 8A.4(B) applies to the Register of Nominees.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.8 Accuracy of and Obligation to Update Nominee Particulars
doc_path: General Rule 8A.8 Accuracy of and Obligation to Update Nominee Particulars
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) A QFC Entity must ensure that the Nominee Particulars in its Register of Nominees are, to the best of its knowledge, adequate, accurate and up-to-date.
(B) If a QFC Entity becomes aware of any change to its Nominee Particulars relating to any of its Nominee Directors or their Nominators or Nominee Shareholders or their Nominators, the QFC Entity must within 15 days of becoming aware of such change:
(i) obtain adequate supporting documentation from each relevant Nominee Director or Nominee Shareholder (as the case may be) evidencing the change, or otherwise verify the accuracy of the change; and
(ii) update its Register of Nominees to reflect the change.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.9 Obligation to Provide Information to the CRO
doc_path: General Rule 8A.9 Obligation to Provide Information to the CRO
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) An Applicant for incorporation or registration within the QFC must submit with its application:
(i) the Basic Information;
(ii) the Required Information relating to each of its proposed Beneficial Owners; and
(iii) if relevant, the Nominee Particulars relating to each of its proposed Nominee Directors and their Nominators and Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators.
(B) A QFC Entity that did not, prior to 5 December 2021, submit a report on its Beneficial Owners to the CRO setting out the Required Information and the Nominee Particulars (if any), must do so by 31 December 2021.
(C) Without prejudice to Rules 8A.5 and 8A.9(A) and (B), the CRO may, in the form and manner it deems appropriate, direct a QFC Entity to submit an annual report on its (i) Basic Information; (ii) Required Information relating to its Beneficial Owners; and (iii) the Nominee Particulars (if relevant) relating to its Nominee Directors and their Nominators and its Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.11 Confidentiality and Security of Beneficial Owner Information and Nominee Particulars
doc_path: General Rule 8A.11 Confidentiality and Security of Beneficial Owner Information and Nominee Particulars
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) A QFC Entity must ensure that its Register of Beneficial Owners and if relevant, its Register of Nominees, are maintained in a manner that protects the security and confidentiality of information.
(B) A QFC Entity must not disclose its Register of Beneficial Owners or any Required Information (and if relevant, its Register of Nominees and the Nominee Particulars), to any Person except if:
(i) the disclosure is permitted or required by law, regulation or rules applicable in the QFC (including the AML/CFT Rules), or the State of Qatar; or
(ii) the relevant Beneficial Owner, Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder or Nominator has given permission for the disclosure.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.12 The Powers of the QFCA to Obtain Documents and Information
doc_path: General Rule 8A.12 The Powers of the QFCA to Obtain Documents and Information
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) In relation to a QFC Entity’s Basic Information, Beneficial Owners, Nominee Directors and their Nominators and Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators, the QFCA may by notice require a Person to produce:
(i) specified information or information of a specified description; or
(ii) specified documents or documents of a specified description,
within a period and in the form and manner that the QFCA reasonably requires.
(B) The QFCA may obtain any information from and enforce any obligations of QFC Entities by virtue of its powers under the QFC Law, the QFC Authority Regulations and the QFCA Rules, including in relation to:
(i) the determination of Beneficial Owners by QFC Entities and the disclosure of Required Information;
(ii) the determination of Nominee Directors and their Nominators and Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators by QFC Entities and the disclosure of the Nominee Particulars; or
(iii) any other information sought by the QFCA from QFC Entities in relation to a QFC Entity’s Basic Information, Beneficial Owners, Nominee Directors and their Nominators, Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators and the Nominee Particulars.
(C) The QFCA may enter the premises of a QFC Entity at any time during Ordinary Business Hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying information relating to:
(i) Basic Information, and the Register of Basic information;
(ii) Beneficial Owners, and the Register of Beneficial Owners; and
(iii) Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders, Nominators and the Register of Nominees;
or related documents stored in any form.

(B) The QFCA may obtain any information from and enforce any obligations of QFC Entities by virtue of its powers under the QFC Law, the QFC Authority Regulations and the QFCA Rules, including in relation to: (i) the determination of Beneficial Owners by QFC Entities and the disclosure of Required Information; (ii) the determination of Nominee Directors and their Nominators and Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators by QFC Entities and the disclosure of the Nominee Particulars; or (iii) any other information sought by the QFCA from QFC Entities in relation to a QFC Entity ’s Basic Information, Beneficial Owners, Nominee Directors and their Nominators, Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators and the Nominee Particulars. (C) The QFCA may enter the premises of a QFC Entity at any time during Ordinary Business Hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying information relating to: (i) Basic Information, and the Register of Basic information; (ii) Beneficial Owners , and the Register of Beneficial Owners ; and (iii) Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders, Nominators and the Register of Nominees; or related documents stored in any form. QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.13 QFCA and CRO Rights to Disclose Information
doc_path: General Rule 8A.13 QFCA and CRO Rights to Disclose Information
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) Neither the QFCA nor CRO will disclose details of Beneficial Owners, Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders or Nominators unless there is:
(i) a statutory obligation or statutory basis to disclose the information; or
(ii) an order of the QFC Court to disclose the information,
and the QFCA or CRO will do so on such terms as they consider appropriate.
(B) In the case of a QFC Entity that has been wound up, dissolved, terminated, struck off or otherwise ceases to exist, the CRO shall retain details of the Basic Information, the Required Information and the Nominee Particulars submitted pursuant to this Rule 8A for a period of 10 years from its winding up, dissolution, termination, striking off or otherwise ceasing to exist.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.15 Exemptions
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
(A) This rule applies to:
(i) a QFC Entity, Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder, or Nominator; or
(ii) a legal person or legal arrangement within the ownership chain of a QFC Entity, Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder or Nominator;
that is:
(iii) a company whose securities are traded on a regulated market that the CRO considers to be subject to adequate requirements in relation to the transparency of ownership information;
(iv) an entity that is regulated by a financial services regulator recognised by the CRO as applying equivalent standards of regulation as those applicable in the QFC;
(v) an entity ultimately owned by a government or government agency or authority, of the State of Qatar or another jurisdiction that the CRO determines from time to time; or
(vi) an entity established under a law of the State of Qatar to perform governmental functions,
(individually “Exempt Person” and collectively “Exempt Persons”)
(B) The requirements of Rules 8A.2 to 8A.11 do not apply to Exempt Persons.
(C) In respect of an Exempt Person, the QFC Entity must:
(i) notify the CRO of the provision of Rule 8A.15(A)(iii) - (vi) that applies to it or to its Nominee Directors (or their Nominators), Nominee Shareholders (or their Nominators) or any legal person or legal arrangement within their ownership chains; and
(ii) provide such other information and documents as the CRO reasonably requires.
(D) A QFC Entity is not required under Rule 8A to make any enquiry about the beneficial ownership of any Exempt Person. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a QFC Entity must record, in its Register of Beneficial Owners, the following Required Information about each Exempt Person (as the case may be):
(i) its full legal name;
(ii) its registered address;
(iii) the provision of Rule 8A.15(A)(iii) to (vi) that applies to it; and
(iv) if it:
(a) has its securities traded on a market referred to in Rule 8A.15(A)(iii), the name of the market;
(b) is regulated by a financial services regulated referred to in Rule 8A.15(A)(iv), the name of the regulator;
(c) is ultimately owned by a government or government agency or authority referred to in Rule 8A.15(A)(v), the name of the government, agency or authority and the jurisdiction in which it is established; or
(d) is established under a law of the State of Qatar referred to in Rule 8A.15(A)(vi) to perform governmental functions, the name of the law.
(E) Rule 8A.15 does not apply to a Person who has an interest in (through shareholding or otherwise) or is otherwise directly or indirectly connected to an Exempt Person unless such Person is an Exempt Person.1

1 An example is if 50% of the shares of a QFC Entity is held by a company which is regulated by a financial service regulator falling within the exemption under 8A.15(A)(iv), and 50% by another company, the exemption applies only to the shareholder which is regulated by that financial services regulator, and the natural persons who are the beneficial owners of the other shareholder company must be identified, verified, registered and disclosed to the CRO in accordance with the provisions of Rule 8A.

Inserted (as from 25th June 2019)

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.16 Issuance of Guidance on Basic Information, Beneficial Owner Information and Nominee Particulars by the QFCA
doc_path: General Rule 8A.16 Issuance of Guidance on Basic Information, Beneficial Owner Information and Nominee Particulars by the QFCA
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
The QFCA may, subject to these Rules, issue guidance, policy statements, forms, procedures, and any other documents or instructions that it considers necessary in relation to:

(A) the determination of Basic Information, Required Information or Nominee Particulars and their content, form and substance;
(B) the manner and form in which QFC Entities must maintain and submit to the CRO their Register of Basic Information, Register of Beneficial Owners or their Register of Nominees, as the case may be;
(C) what constitutes Basic Information, Required Information or Nominee Particulars;
(D) the definition of a Beneficial Owner, Nominee Director, Nominee Shareholder or Nominator;
(E) the manner and form in which the Register of Basic Information, Register of Beneficial Owners or the Register of Nominees is obtained by the CRO;
(F) the regulated markets, financial services regulators or the other jurisdictions referred to in Rule 8A.15(A); and
(G) any other matter relating to the determination and disclosure of Basic Information, Beneficial Owners, Nominee Directors, Nominee Shareholders or Nominators, as the case may be, of QFC Entities subject to the limitations of its authority as set out in the QFC Law, the QFCA Regulations and the QFCA Rules.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 8A.17 Record Keeping
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Members of the Governing Body of a QFC Entity jointly and severally must maintain the following information for a period of ten (10) years from the date that the QFC Entity is dissolved, wound up, terminated, struck off or otherwise ceases to exist:

(i) the Basic Information and the Register of Basic Information relating to the QFC Entity;
(ii) the Required Information relating to its Beneficial Owners and Register of Beneficial Owners; and
(iii) where relevant, the Nominee Particulars relating to its Nominee Directors and their Nominators, Nominee Shareholders and their Nominators and Register of Nominees.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 9.2 Accounting Records
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: General Rule 9.2 Accounting Records

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 9.2.1
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A Licensed Firm must keep accounting records with respect to all sums of money received and expended by the Licensed Firm and all sales and purchases of goods and services and other transactions by the Licensed Firm and the assets and liabilities of the Licensed Firm. Such accounting records must be sufficient to show and explain all transactions by the Licensed Firm and must be such to:

(A) disclose with reasonable accuracy the financial position of the Licensed Firm at any time;
(B) enable the Licensed Firm to ensure that any accounts prepared by the Licensed Firm comply with the requirements in these Rules; and
(C) record the financial position of the Licensed Firm as at its financial year end.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 9.4.1
doc_path: General Rule 9.4 Financial Accounts and Statements
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Within four months of the end of the financial year, a Licensed Firm must:

(A) have its accounts and financial statements examined and reported upon by the Licensed Firm's auditor in accordance with the requirements of the Companies Regulations or Limited Liability Partnership Regulations, any other applicable Regulations and these Rules; and
(B) file a copy of the financial statements and auditor's report with the CRO.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 9.5 Auditor's Report
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: General Rule 9.5 Auditor's Report

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 9.5.1
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A Licensed Firm must in addition to the requirements contained in the Companies Regulations, the Limited Liability Partnership Regulations, and other applicable Regulations ensure that its auditor:

(A) conducts an audit of the Licensed Firm's accounts and financial statements in accordance with the requirements of the relevant standards published by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB) or other standards deemed acceptable by the QFCA;
(B) produces a report on the audited accounts and financial statements which states:
(i) whether, in the auditor's opinion, the accounts have been properly prepared in accordance with the requirements imposed by Regulations or these Rules;
(ii) in particular, whether the accounts give a true and fair view of the financial position of the Licensed Firm for the financial year and of the state of the Licensed Firm's affairs at its financial year end; and
(iii) any other matter or opinion relating to the requirements of Regulations or these Rules;
(C) produce an auditors report which states whether:
(i) the auditor has audited the Licensed Firm's annual financial statements in accordance with the IAASB or other standards deemed acceptable by the QFCA;
(ii) the auditor has carried out any other procedures considered necessary, having regard to the IAASB or other standards deemed acceptable by the QFCA;
(iii) the auditor has received all necessary information and explanations for the purposes of preparing this report to the QFCA; and
(iv) in the auditor's opinion, the Licensed Firm has kept proper accounting records, in compliance with the applicable Rules;
(D) produces, if the Licensed Firm controls or holds Client Money, a report which states whether, in the opinion of the Auditor:
(i) the Licensed Firm has maintained throughout the year systems and controls to enable it to comply with the relevant provisions of the LFAR;
(ii) the Licensed Firm's controls are such as to ensure that Client Money is identifiable and secure at all times;
(iii) any of the requirements of LFAR have not been met;
(iv) if applicable, Client Money that has been segregated in accordance with the LFAR;
(v) if applicable, the Licensed Firm was holding and controlling an appropriate amount of Client Money in accordance with LFAR as at the date on which the Licensed Firm's audited balance sheet was prepared; and
(vi) if applicable, there have been any material discrepancies in the reconciliation of Client Money.

(B) produces a report on the audited accounts and financial statements which states: (i) whether, in the auditor's opinion, the accounts have been properly prepared in accordance with the requirements imposed by Regulations or these Rules ; (ii) in particular, whether the accounts give a true and fair view of the financial position of the Licensed Firm for the financial year and of the state of the Licensed Firm's affairs at its financial year end; and (iii) any other matter or opinion relating to the requirements of Regulations or these Rules ; (C) produce an auditors report which states whether: (i) the auditor has audited the Licensed Firm's annual financial statements in accordance with the IAASB or other standards deemed acceptable by the QFCA ; (ii) the auditor has carried out any other procedures considered necessary, having regard to the IAASB or other standards deemed acceptable by the QFCA ; (iii) the auditor has received all necessary information and explanations for the purposes of preparing this report to the QFCA ; and (iv) in the auditor's opinion, the Licensed Firm has kept proper accounting records, in compliance with the applicable Rules ; (D) produces, if the Licensed Firm controls or holds Client Money , a report which states whether, in the opinion of the Auditor: (i) the Licensed Firm has maintained throughout the year systems and controls to enable it to comply with the relevant provisions of the LFAR ; and (vi) if applicable, there have been any material discrepancies in the reconciliation of Client Money .

Should a Licensed Firm fail to pay by the due date then, without limiting the right of the QFCA to take any other action, the sum due will be increased by 1% for each calendar month, or part of a calendar month, that it remains outstanding beyond the due date.

General Rule 12.3 Consideration of Registered Function Notices
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
The QFCA shall advise of any objections to the Registered Function Notice or conditions to the acceptance of the Registered Function Notice no later than thirty (30) days following the date of delivery of a complete Registered Function Notice to the QFCA. If the QFCA does not send any objections or notice of conditions in writing to the Licensed Firm within thirty (30) days following such date the Registered Function Notice shall be deemed to have been accepted unconditionally by the QFCA. If the QFCA does advise the Licensed Firm of any objections or conditions of acceptance then it may call for such further information from the Licensed Firm and such other parties as it considers necessary or appropriate, and shall make a final determination within thirty (30) days of receipt of such information.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: General Rule 13.2.1
doc_path: General Rule 13.2 Licensed Firm's Assessment of Individuals
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
Before registering an individual as conducting a Registered Function with the QFCA, a Licensed Firm must make reasonable enquiries as to an individual's fitness and propriety to carry out a Registered Function. When making an assessment of an individual to determine the fitness and propriety of the individual, a Licensed Firm should have regard to the individual's:

(A) honesty, integrity and reputation;
(B) competence and capability; and
(C) financial soundness.
