QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Part 8: Token Service Providers’ Code
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Part 8: Token Service Providers’ Code

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 1. Application
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
The QFCA Rules in this Part 8 shall be referred to as the “Token Service Providers’ Code” and shall apply to all TSPs.

Definitions

In this Token Service Providers’ Code:

“Client” means any Person who enters into a transaction with a TSP;

“Governing Body” means:

(a) for a company or a company limited by guarantee, its board of directors;
(b) for a limited partnership, its general partner;
(c) for a trust, its trustee or trustees;
(d) for a foundation, its council; and
(e) for any other entity, its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body,

“Permitted Token” has the meaning set out in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024; and

“Token Infrastructure” has the meaning set out in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: The QFCA Rules in this Part 8 shall be referred to as the “ Token Service Providers’ Code ” and shall apply to all TSPs. Definitions In this Token Service Providers’ Code : “ Client ” means any Person who enters into a transaction with a TSP; “ Governing Body ” means: (a) for a company or a company limited by guarantee, its board of directors; (b) for a limited partnership, its general partner; (c) for a trust, its trustee or trustees; (d) for a foundation, its council; and (e) for any other entity, its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body, “ Permitted Token ” has the meaning set out in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024; and “ Token Infrastructure ” has the meaning set out in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 2. Client Terms and Conditions
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must not carry on a Token Service for aClient unless:

(A) the TSP has terms and conditions containing key information about provision of the service; and
(B) the TSP provides the terms and conditions to theClient in sufficient time to enable theClient to make an informed decision about the provision of the service by the TSP (unless the TSP can demonstrate that it is impracticable to provide the terms and conditions in that time frame in the circumstances, in which case the TSP must provide the terms and conditions to theClient as soon as is reasonably practicable).
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must not carry on a Token Service for a Client unless: (A) the TSP has terms and conditions containing key information about provision of the service; and (B) the TSP provides the terms and conditions to the Client in sufficient time to enable the Client to make an informed decision about the provision of the service by the TSP (unless the TSP can demonstrate that it is impracticable to provide the terms and conditions in that time frame in the circumstances, in which case the TSP must provide the terms and conditions to the Client as soon as is reasonably practicable).

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 3. Risk Disclosure
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html: A TSP must not carry on a Token Service for aClient unless the TSP has disclosed to theClient all material risks related to the service before providing the service to theClient (or, if the TSP can demonstrate that it is impracticable to do so beforehand, as soon as is reasonably practicable).
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must not carry on a Token Service for a Client unless the TSP has disclosed to the Client all material risks related to the service before providing the service to the Client (or, if the TSP can demonstrate that it is impracticable to do so beforehand, as soon as is reasonably practicable).

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: 4. Management, Systems and Controls
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: 4. Management, Systems and Controls

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Governing body and senior management responsibilities
doc_path: Governing body and senior management responsibilities
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Governing body and senior management responsibilities

doc_path: Governing body and senior management responsibilities
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must:

(A) appropriately apportion its significant responsibilities between the members of itsGoverning Body and its senior management;

(B) allocate to the individual registered to carry out the TSP’s Senior Executive Function the functions of:

(i) apportioning significant responsibilities; and
(ii) overseeing the establishment and maintenance of systems and controls;
(C) establish, maintain and regularly review systems and controls, appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the TSP’s operations, that ensure the TSP’s affairs are managed effectively and responsibly by its senior management;

(D) establish and implement appropriate measures to ensure that:

(i) the roles and responsibilities assigned to the TSP’sGoverning Body are clearly defined; and
(ii) to the extent that roles and responsibilities are delegated by the Governing Body, there are clear reporting lines applicable to the individuals to whom any aspect of those roles and responsibilities is delegated; and
(E) ensure that key duties and functions are segregated such that duties and functions to be performed by the same individual do not conflict with each other.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must: (A) appropriately apportion its significant responsibilities between the members of its Governing Body and its senior management; (B) allocate to the individual registered to carry out the TSP’s Senior Executive Function the functions of: (i) apportioning significant responsibilities; and (ii) overseeing the establishment and maintenance of systems and controls; (C) establish, maintain and regularly review systems and controls, appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the TSP’s operations, that ensure the TSP’s affairs are managed effectively and responsibly by its senior management; (D) establish and implement appropriate measures to ensure that: (i) the roles and responsibilities assigned to the TSP’s Governing Body are clearly defined; and (ii) to the extent that roles and responsibilities are delegated by the Governing Body , there are clear reporting lines applicable to the individuals to whom any aspect of those roles and responsibilities is delegated; and (E) ensure that key duties and functions are segregated such that duties and functions to be performed by the same individual do not conflict with each other.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Risk management, including technology risks
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Risk management, including technology risks

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must establish and maintain risk management systems and controls to enable it to identify, assess, mitigate, control and monitor its material risks, including in relation to the risks of inadequately providing for:

(A) the maintenance and development of systems and architecture (including code version control, implementation of updates, issue resolution, and regular internal and third party testing);
(B) security measures and procedures for the safe storage and transmission of data, including in relation to the protection and encryption of passwords, keys or other means of access or verification;
(C) business continuity and client-engagement planning in the event of both planned and unplanned system outages;
(D) procedures for the creation and management of services, interfaces and channels provided by or to third parties (as recipients and providers of data or services); and
(E) the management and active testing of changes in the underlying protocol or programming of aPermitted Token orToken Infrastructure upon which aPermitted Token is generated (including those that result in a fork in the infrastructure).
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must establish and maintain risk management systems and controls to enable it to identify, assess, mitigate, control and monitor its material risks, including in relation to the risks of inadequately providing for: (A) the maintenance and development of systems and architecture (including code version control, implementation of updates, issue resolution, and regular internal and third party testing); (B) security measures and procedures for the safe storage and transmission of data, including in relation to the protection and encryption of passwords, keys or other means of access or verification; (C) business continuity and client-engagement planning in the event of both planned and unplanned system outages; (D) procedures for the creation and management of services, interfaces and channels provided by or to third parties (as recipients and providers of data or services); and (E) the management and active testing of changes in the underlying protocol or programming of a Permitted Token or Token Infrastructure upon which a Permitted Token is generated (including those that result in a fork in the infrastructure).

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Compliance and internal audit
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Compliance and internal audit

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must:

(A) establish and maintain compliance arrangements, including processes and procedures to ensure that the TSP complies with all applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC;
(B) appoint an individual as compliance officer with responsibility for monitoring the TSP’s compliance with all applicable laws, regulations and rules and for taking steps to ensure such compliance;

(C) ensure that the compliance officer has:

(i) access to sufficient resources to perform their duties objectively and independently of operational and business functions; and
(ii) unrestricted access to relevant records and to theGoverning Body and senior management;
(D) establish and maintain monitoring and reporting processes and procedures to ensure that any compliance breaches are readily identified, reported and promptly acted upon;
(E) establish and maintain an independent internal audit function with responsibility for monitoring the appropriateness and effectiveness of the TSP’s processes, procedures, systems and controls, including conducting a review, at least annually, of theToken Infrastructure and other technology used by the TSP; and
(F) establish and maintain arrangements to provide the TSP’sGoverning Body and senior management with the information necessary to organise, monitor and control its activities, as well as comply with applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC and to manage risks.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must: (A) establish and maintain compliance arrangements, including processes and procedures to ensure that the TSP complies with all applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC; (B) appoint an individual as compliance officer with responsibility for monitoring the TSP’s compliance with all applicable laws, regulations and rules and for taking steps to ensure such compliance; (C) ensure that the compliance officer has: (i) access to sufficient resources to perform their duties objectively and independently of operational and business functions; and (ii) unrestricted access to relevant records and to the Governing Body and senior management; (D) establish and maintain monitoring and reporting processes and procedures to ensure that any compliance breaches are readily identified, reported and promptly acted upon; (E) establish and maintain an independent internal audit function with responsibility for monitoring the appropriateness and effectiveness of the TSP’s processes, procedures, systems and controls, including conducting a review, at least annually, of the Token Infrastructure and other technology used by the TSP; and (F) establish and maintain arrangements to provide the TSP’s Governing Body and senior management with the information necessary to organise, monitor and control its activities, as well as comply with applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC and to manage risks.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Staff conduct
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Staff conduct

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must:

(A) ensure that its employees are fit and proper to perform the functions assigned to them; and
(B) establish and maintain systems and controls to ensure that the TSP and its employees do not engage in conduct constituting a crime under any laws of the State.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must: (A) ensure that its employees are fit and proper to perform the functions assigned to them; and (B) establish and maintain systems and controls to ensure that the TSP and its employees do not engage in conduct constituting a crime under any laws of the State.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Outsourcing
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Outsourcing

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html: A TSP must inform the QFCA about any arrangements whereby the TSP outsources any of its functions or activities directly related to the Token Services it provides (including its internal audit function, or any part of it).
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP must inform the QFCA about any arrangements whereby the TSP outsources any of its functions or activities directly related to the Token Services it provides (including its internal audit function, or any part of it).

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html: A TSP may outsource its internal audit function, or any part of it, only if authorised to do so by itsGoverning Body.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP may outsource its internal audit function, or any part of it, only if authorised to do so by its Governing Body .

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html: A TSP that outsources any such function or activity is not relieved of its regulatory obligations and remains responsible for compliance with applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC in relation to any outsourced function or activity.
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP that outsources any such function or activity is not relieved of its regulatory obligations and remains responsible for compliance with applicable laws, regulations and rules in the QFC in relation to any outsourced function or activity.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html: A TSP considering outsourcing such a function or activity must, when assessing any potential third party service provider, satisfy itself that the service provider maintains robust processes and procedures regarding the function or activity to be outsourced (including, for example, in relation to testing and technology security).
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: A TSP considering outsourcing such a function or activity must, when assessing any potential third party service provider, satisfy itself that the service provider maintains robust processes and procedures regarding the function or activity to be outsourced (including, for example, in relation to testing and technology security).

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Information security
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Information security

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must:

(A) establish and maintain a plan describing the security arrangements relating to:

(i) Permitted Tokens in relation to which the TSP carries on a Token Service;
(ii) any keys or other means of verification related to those Permitted Tokens;
(iii) the privacy of sensitive personal data (within the meaning given by the QFC Data Protection Regulations);
(iv) the TSP’s networks and systems and any other networks or systems utilised by the TSP;
(v) any cloud-based services utilised by the TSP;
(vi) the TSP’s physical facilities; and
(vii) documents and document storage;
(B) establish and maintain policies and procedures to ensure the TSP acts in accordance with the QFC Data Protection Regulations and QFC Data Protection Rules;

(C) establish and maintain policies and procedures for recovery in the event that:

(i) aclient loses access to their credentials or the security of those credentials is compromised; or
(ii) a key, or other means of access, for Permitted Tokens in relation to which the TSP carries on a Token Service are lost or the security of the key, or other means of access, is compromised;
(D) take steps to ensure that public and private cloud-service providers utilised by the TSP do not expose the TSP to security risks;
(E) establish and maintain a set of well-defined and documented access management procedures;
(F) annually review all service level agreements with third party providers for serviceability and security of the systems;
(G) have clearly defined roles and responsibilities delineating the operations of any third party service provider from those of the TSP;
(H) limit physical access to systems to the relevant personnel and access and monitor such access on an ongoing basis; and
(I) store, and be in the position to retrieve, data held on a cloud platform utilised by the TSP for such duration as required under any relevant regulations, these QFCA Rules and any other relevant rules.

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.title: Whistle-blower protections
QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.content_text: Whistle-blower protections

QFCA Rules :: QFCA Rules.document_html:
A TSP must establish and maintain appropriate policies and procedures to:

(A) facilitate the reporting by any individual of concerns relating to the TSP’s compliance with these Rules and any other applicable laws, regulations or rules; and
(B) where such concerns are reported, assess and, where appropriate, escalate them.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 1 General Provisions
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 1 General Provisions

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 1.1 Application
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: These Rules apply to every Person to whom the Single Family Office Regulations apply.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: These Rules apply to every Person to whom the Single Family Office Regulations apply.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 1.2 Purpose
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
The purpose of these Rules is to provide further detail in respect of the operation of the Single Family Office Regulations and to provide in particular for:

(A) the licensing of Single Family Offices by the QFC Authority;
(B) the recognition of Eligible Firms;
(C) the procedure for amending the Articles of Association of a Single Family Office;
(D) the requirements on a Single Family Office before it registers a transfer of Shares; and
(E) the process by which the CRO may revoke the registration of a Company as a Single Family Office.

These Rules should be read in conjunction with the Single Family Office Regulations.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: The purpose of these Rules is to provide further detail in respect of the operation of the Single Family Office Regulations and to provide in particular for: (A) the licensing of Single Family Offices by the QFC Authority; (B) the recognition of Eligible Firms; (C) the procedure for amending the Articles of Association of a Single Family Office; (D) the requirements on a Single Family Office before it registers a transfer of Shares; and (E) the process by which the CRO may revoke the registration of a Company as a Single Family Office. These Rules should be read in conjunction with the Single Family Office Regulations.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 1.3 Interpretation
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
In these Rules:

(A) defined terms are identified by the capitalisation of the initial letter of the word or phrase; and
(B) defined terms have the same meaning as they have in the Single Family Office Regulations, QFC Companies Regulations, QFC Authority Regulations, QFCA Rules, any other related QFC regulations or rules as relevant to the context in which they are used.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2 Single Family Offices
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2 Single Family Offices

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.1 Key terms
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2.1 Key terms

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.1.1 What is a Single Family Office?
doc_path: 2.1.1 What is a Single Family Office?
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: A Single Family Office is a body corporate established within the QFC for the sole purpose of providing services to and carrying on activities in relation to a Single Family in accordance with the Single Family Office Regulations.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: A Single Family Office is a body corporate established within the QFC for the sole purpose of providing services to and carrying on activities in relation to a Single Family in accordance with the Single Family Office Regulations.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.1.2 What is a Single Family?
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
A Single Family is a family made up of a group of individuals all of whom are the bloodline descendants of a common ancestor or their spouses (including widows and widowers, whether or not remarried), and subject to such other limitations or conditions agreed with or specified by the QFC Authority.

Note: The Single Family Office Regulations provide further definitions for "Family Entity" and "Family Fiduciary Structure".

Note: The Single Family Office Regulations provide further definitions for "Family Entity" and "Family Fiduciary Structure".

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.1.3 Who is a Designated Representative?
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: A Designated Representative is a natural person appointed by a Single Family Office in accordance with Article 20 of the Single Family Office Regulations to act as a point of contact for the QFC Authority. The function of the Designated Representative is a Registered Function for the purpose of the QFCA Rules.

The function of the Designated Representative is a Registered Function for the purpose of the QFCA Rules.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.2 Basic Concepts
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2.2 Basic Concepts

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.2.1 Scope of Licence
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: A Single Family Office may only carry out SFO Activities to the extent that it is permitted to carry out such activities under its Licence. A Single Family Office may not carry on any Regulated Activity in or from the QFC without the prior authorisation of the Regulatory Authority. A Single Family Office may only provide services to a Single Family and must not hold itself out to or solicit business from third parties.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: A Single Family Office may only carry out SFO Activities to the extent that it is permitted to carry out such activities under its Licence. A Single Family Office may not carry on any Regulated Activity in or from the QFC without the prior authorisation of the Regulatory Authority. A Single Family Office may only provide services to a Single Family and must not hold itself out to or solicit business from third parties.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.3 Key Requirements
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2.3 Key Requirements

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.3.1 Licence
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: An application to the QFC Authority for a Licence to conduct SFO Activities must be accompanied by a letter from an Eligible Firm which confirms that various threshold conditions for the granting of a Licence have been fulfilled. The Rules in 2.4 set out the process for seeking a Licence, the criteria that the QFC Authority will apply in determining whether to grant a Licence and the conditions pursuant to which an entity in or outside the QFC may act as an Eligible Firm.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: An application to the QFC Authority for a Licence to conduct SFO Activities must be accompanied by a letter from an Eligible Firm which confirms that various threshold conditions for the granting of a Licence have been fulfilled. The Rules in 2.4 set out the process for seeking a Licence, the criteria that the QFC Authority will apply in determining whether to grant a Licence and the conditions pursuant to which an entity in or outside the QFC may act as an Eligible Firm.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.3.2 Registration
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
A Company may be registered by the CRO as a Single Family Office under Article 16 of the Single Family Office Regulations if:

(A) it fulfils all the requirements for incorporation under the Companies Regulations;
(B) it fulfils the requirements under the Single Family Office Regulations, namely the requirements under Article 19 relating to the Articles of Association of the Company; and
(C) it has received a Licence from the QFC Authority to conduct SFO Activities.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: A Company may be registered by the CRO as a Single Family Office under Article 16 of the Single Family Office Regulations if: (A) it fulfils all the requirements for incorporation under the Companies Regulations; (B) it fulfils the requirements under the Single Family Office Regulations, namely the requirements under Article 19 relating to the Articles of Association of the Company; and (C) it has received a Licence from the QFC Authority to conduct SFO Activities.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.3.3 Designated Representative
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html: A Single Family Office is obliged to appoint a Designated Representative to act as a point of contact with the QFC Authority. The appointment of the Designated Representative is not subject to the approval of the QFC Authority but the Single Family Office is required to ensure that the proposed person meets certain criteria. The QFC Authority may require the Single Family Office to appoint an alternative Designated Representative if for any reason it considers that a Designated Representative does not satisfy or has ceased to satisfy these criteria.

The QFC Authority may require the Single Family Office to appoint an alternative Designated Representative if for any reason it considers that a Designated Representative does not satisfy or has ceased to satisfy these criteria.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.4 Licence to conduct SFO Activities
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2.4 Licence to conduct SFO Activities

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.4.1 Application to conduct SFO Activities
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
An applicant seeking permission to conduct SFO Activities must:

(A) complete the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) attach a letter from an Eligible Firm complying with the requirements of Article 18 of the Single Family Office Regulations;
(C) attach a statement signed by the applicant or its Designated Representative containing the information set out in Article 15.5 of the Single Family Office Regulations;
(D) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority; and
(E) pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: An applicant seeking permission to conduct SFO Activities must: (A) complete the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority; (B) attach a letter from an Eligible Firm complying with the requirements of Article 18 of the Single Family Office Regulations; (C) attach a statement signed by the applicant or its Designated Representative containing the information set out in Article 15.5 of the Single Family Office Regulations; (D) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority; and (E) pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.4.2 Eligible Firm
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
1) For the purposes of Articles 18 and 22.2 of the Single Family Office Regulations an Eligible Firm means:
(A) an entity established in the QFC with a Licence to provide accounting, tax, legal or management services:
(B) subject to (2), an entity established in the QFC with a Licence to provide services other than those stated in (A);
(C) subject to (3), an entity established in a jurisdiction other than the QFC.
2) Before the QFC Authority recognises a letter issued by an entity established in the QFC with a Licence to provide services other than those stated in (1)(A), the incorporators (in the case of Article 18) or the Single Family Office (in the case of Article 22.2) must satisfy the QFC Authority that:
(A) the entity has the necessary expertise to opine on the matters stated in the letter required by either Article 18 or Article 22.2 as appropriate;
(B) the entity has adequate professional indemnity insurance which provides cover in respect of the work required; and
(C) it meets any other requirements prescribed by the QFC Authority.
3) Before the QFC Authority recognises a letter issued by an entity established outside the QFC, the incorporators (in the case of Article 18) or the Single Family Office (in the case of Article 22.2) must satisfy the QFC Authority that:
(A) the entity has the necessary expertise to opine on the matters stated in the letter required by either Article 18 or Article 22.2 as appropriate;
(B) the entity is subject in its home jurisdiction to licensing and ongoing monitoring of the relevant aspects of its activities;
(C) the body or bodies that granted the entity's licence and monitors its activities are able to exercise sufficient disciplinary actions over the applicant;
(D) the entity has adequate professional indemnity insurance which provides cover in respect of work undertaken in the QFC; and
(E) the entity meets any other requirements prescribed by the QFC Authority.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.4.3 Licensing Criteria
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
When assessing an application to conduct SFO Activities, the QFC Authority may consider any of the following criteria, as well as any other criteria which in its sole discretion it considers relevant in order to further the QFC Authority's Objectives as set out in Article 5 of the QFC Law:

(A) the background and history of the applicant;
(B) the fitness and propriety of the individual performing the Designated Representative function;
(C) the fitness and propriety of the Persons who control the applicant;
(D) the professional memberships, if any, held by individuals employed by the applicant;
(E) the ownership of the applicant, including the identity of all Persons who control the applicant;
(F) with respect to the holding of Client Money, the procedures by which it proposes to ensure compliance with LFAR;
(G) the adequacy of business continuity arrangements and IT systems upon which the applicant intends to rely; and
(H) such other criteria as the QFC Authority may consider relevant or necessary.
Amended (as from 12 November 2025).

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.5 Designated Representative
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 2.5 Designated Representative

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 2.5.1 Application of General Rules
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
A Single Family Office must comply with the following General Rules in the QFCA Rules in respect of a Designated Representative:

(A) 12 Notification of Registered Functions;
(B) 13 Fitness and Propriety;
(C) 14 Competence, Training and Supervision; and
(D) 15 Performance of Registered Functions.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 3 Change of Status
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 3 Change of Status

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 3.1 Amendments to Articles of Association
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
1) Article 19.5 provides that a Single Family Office must give no less than twenty-one days' prior written notice to the QFC Authority of any proposal to amend its Articles of Association and that the QFC Authority may consult with the QFC Authority and Regulatory Authority as appropriate and object to the proposed amendment if it is not in line with the status of a Single Family Office.
2) A Single Family Office must provide notice to the QFC Authority of such proposed amendment using the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
3) The Single Family Office's application must include:
(A) a copy of the proposed amended Articles of Association;
(B) a detailed description of the reasons for the proposed amendment;
(C) confirmation that the proposed amended Articles of Association still comply with the requirements of Article 19.2 and 19.3; and
(D) an explanation as to why the proposed amendment is in line with the status of the Company as a Single Family Office.
4) The twenty-one day period prescribed in Article 19.5 will not begin until the Single Family Office submits an application conforming in all respects to the above criteria.
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.content_text: 1) Article 19.5 provides that a Single Family Office must give no less than twenty-one days' prior written notice to the QFC Authority of any proposal to amend its Articles of Association and that the QFC Authority may consult with the QFC Authority and Regulatory Authority as appropriate and object to the proposed amendment if it is not in line with the status of a Single Family Office. 2) A Single Family Office must provide notice to the QFC Authority of such proposed amendment using the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority. 3) The Single Family Office's application must include: (A) a copy of the proposed amended Articles of Association; (B) a detailed description of the reasons for the proposed amendment; (C) confirmation that the proposed amended Articles of Association still comply with the requirements of Article 19.2 and 19.3 ; and (D) an explanation as to why the proposed amendment is in line with the status of the Company as a Single Family Office. 4) The twenty-one day period prescribed in Article 19.5 will not begin until the Single Family Office submits an application conforming in all respects to the above criteria.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 3.2 Revocation of registration as a Single Family Office
doc_path: 3.2 Revocation of registration as a Single Family Office
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
1) The CRO may revoke the registration of a Company as a Single Family Office:
(A) on the application of the Single Family Office itself if the condition in (3) is met; or
(B) on the application of the QFC Authority.
2) The CRO shall revoke the registration of a Company as a Single Family Office by amending the public register so as to remove the words "SFO Activities" from the section indicating the business activities of the Company.
3) A Single Family Office may not apply to the CRO for the revocation of its registration as a Single Family Office until it has complied with Article 26.3 (a) to (d) of the Single Family Office Regulations and been issued with an amended Licence by the QFC Authority and, where applicable, an authorisation by the QFC Regulatory Authority.
4) A Single Family Office applying to the CRO for the revocation of its registration as a Single Family Office must:
(A) complete the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and file it with the CRO;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the CRO; and
(C) pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the CRO.
5) The CRO may not deregister a Single Family Office on the application of the Single Family Office itself unless it has received written notice from the QFC Authority confirming that the Single Family Office is no longer performing SFO Activities.

QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.title: 3.3 Transfer of Shares
QFCA Rules :: Single Family Office Rules.document_html:
1) Article 19.4 of the Single Family Office Regulations provides that the Articles of Association of a Single Family Office must provide that no transfer of shares in the Single Family Office shall take effect unless the QFC Authority has confirmed in writing that it is satisfied that the transfer will not affect the status of the Single Family Office.
2) A Single Family Office applying for the QFC Authority's confirmation under Article 19.4 must:
(A) complete the Prescribed Form in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority; and
(C) pay the Prescribed Fee stated in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
3) Before the QFC Authority confirms that it does not object to such a transfer, the Single Family Office must satisfy the QFC Authority that the proposed transfer will not affect the status of the Single Family Office.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 1. General Provisions
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.content_text: 1. General Provisions

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 1.1. Application
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html: These Rules apply to every Person to whom the QFC Special Company Regulations apply.
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.content_text: These Rules apply to every Person to whom the QFC Special Company Regulations apply.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 1.2. Purpose of these Rules
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
The purpose of these Rules is to provide further detail in respect of the operation of the QFC Special Company Regulations and to provide in particular for:

(A) the incorporation, licensing and registration of Special Companies;
(B) the approval of Support Services Providers;
(C) the application of various aspects of the QFC Companies Regulations and QFC Insolvency Regulations to Special Companies; and
(D) various notification requirements placed upon Special Companies by the QFC Authority and the CRO.

These Rules should be read in conjunction with the QFC Special Company Regulations.

Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

These Rules should be read in conjunction with the QFC Special Company Regulations. Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 1.3. Interpretation
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
In these Rules:

(A) defined terms are identified by the capitalisation of the initial letter of the word or phrase; and
(B) defined terms have the same meaning as they have in the QFC Special Company Regulations, the QFC Insolvency Regulations, the QFC Companies Regulations, the QFC Authority Regulations, the QFCA Rules, any other related QFC regulations or rules as relevant to the context in which they are used.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.1.1. What is a Special Purpose Company?
doc_path: 2.1.1. What is a Special Purpose Company?
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
A Special Purpose Company is a company incorporated under the QFC Companies Regulations and registered by the CRO as a Special Purpose Company. A Special Purpose Company may only be established for the Purpose of a Transaction.

Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

A Special Purpose Company may only be established for the Purpose of a Transaction. Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.1.2. What are Special Purpose Company Activities?
doc_path: 2.1.2. What are Special Purpose Company Activities?
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
Subject to the terms of its Licence, a Special Purpose Company may only carry out one or more of the Special Purpose Company Activities set out in Article 9 of the QFC Special Company Regulations.

Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.1.3. What is a Support Services Provider?
doc_path: 2.1.3. What is a Support Services Provider?
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
A Support Services Provider is a body corporate, partnership or limited liability partnership approved by the QFC Authority to provide Corporate and Administrative Services to a Special Company.

Amended (as from 19th October 2017).
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.content_text: A Support Services Provider is a body corporate, partnership or limited liability partnership approved by the QFC Authority to provide Corporate and Administrative Services to a Special Company. Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.1.4. What are Corporate and Administrative Services?
doc_path: 2.1.4. What are Corporate and Administrative Services?
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
In relation to a Support Services Provider, Corporate and Administrative Services include:

(A) management and administrative services;
(B) services as a registered agent, director or similar officer (including, where permitted, to provide the Senior Executive Function);
(C) provision of a registered office, place of business or address; and
(D) (D) any of the services above, and such other services as may be prescribed or directed from time to time by the QFC Authority.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.content_text: 2.2 Basic Concepts

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.2.1. Scope of Licence
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html: A Special Purpose Company may only carry out Special Purpose Company Activities to the extent that it is permitted to carry out such activities under its Licence. A Special Purpose Company may not carry on any Regulated Activities in or from the QFC without the prior authorisation of the Regulatory Authority.

A Special Purpose Company may not carry on any Regulated Activities in or from the QFC without the prior authorisation of the Regulatory Authority.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.2.2. Application of the QFC Companies Regulations
doc_path: 2.2.2. Application of the QFC Companies Regulations
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.2.3. Application of the QFC Insolvency Regulations
doc_path: 2.2.3. Application of the QFC Insolvency Regulations
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
A Special Purpose Company is subject to the provisions of the QFC Insolvency Regulations, subject to certain modifications and exemptions:

(A) a Special Purpose Company can only be wound up voluntarily under Article 58 if it has no outstanding liabilities;
(B) in relation to a Special Purpose Company, any reference to "the Company's property" is a reference to any property of the Special Purpose Company other than property under administration;
(C) a Special Purpose Company has no preferential debts or preferential creditors within the meaning of Article 148;
(D) Special Purpose Company Activities and any obligations arising from such activities are exempt from the liquidator's power to disclaim onerous property under Article 92; and
(E) a Special Purpose Company is exempt from Article 143 (Preferences) and Article 145 (Invalid security interests).
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html: A Licence to conduct Special Purpose Company Activities may be granted by the QFC Authority. A Special Purpose Company is exempt from certain licensing requirements ordinarily applied to Companies by the QFC Authority, including the requirement to maintain physical office space in the QFC where a registered address in the QFC can be provided by its Support Services Provider. QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.3.3 Support Services Provider
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
Subject to Article 27.2 of the QFC Special Company Regulations, a Special Purpose Company is required to appoint and retain at all times a Support Services Provider to provide it with one or more Corporate and Administrative Services, and such other services as may be prescribed or directed from time to time by the QFC Authority. A Support Services Provider may be a body corporate, a partnership or a limited liability partnership established either inside or outside the QFC but in either case must be approved by the QFC Authority. Rules as to the process by which the QFC Authority will approve Support Services Providers are set out at 2.5.2.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.4.2 Licensing Criteria
doc_path: 2.4 Licence to conduct Special Purpose Company Activities
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
When assessing an application to conduct Special Purpose Company Activities, the QFC Authority may consider any of the following criteria, as well as any other criteria which in its sole discretion considers relevant in order to further the QFC Authority's objectives as set out in Article 5 of the QFC Law:

(A) the background and history of the applicant;
(B) the fitness and propriety of individuals performing the Senior Executive Function;
(C) the fitness and propriety of the persons who Control the applicant (for this purpose Control has the meaning set out in the QFCA Rules, Part 2 - General Rules, Rule 8.2.1);
(D) the ownership of the applicant, including the identity and details of the Beneficial Owners of the applicant;
(E) whether the Purpose of the Transaction is in the interests of the QFC or likely to be beneficial to the development of the QFC; and
(F) such other criteria as the QFC Authority may consider relevant or necessary.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.5.1 Register of Approved Support Services Providers
doc_path: 2.5.1 Register of Approved Support Services Providers
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
The CRO will maintain the register of approved Support Services Providers by recording the following information in respect of current and former registered approved Support Services Providers:

(B) address;

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.5.2 Approved Support Services Provider
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) The following categories of applicants may apply to the QFC Authority to be entered on the register of approved Support Services Providers maintained by the CRO:
(A) a body corporate incorporated in the QFC or a partnership or limited liability partnership established in the QFC with, in each case, a Licence to conduct the Permitted Activities set out in paragraphs 12, 13 and 14 of Schedule 3 of the QFC Law; and
(B) subject to 2.5.2 (4), a body corporate, partnership or limited liability partnership established in a jurisdiction other than the QFC.
(2) In making an application under 2.5.2 (1) to be registered, an applicant must:
(A) complete the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority; and
(C) pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
(3) Subject to 2.5.2 (4), before the QFC Authority approves an applicant to appear on the register an applicant must satisfy the QFC Authority that:
(A) it is fit and proper to be registered as a Support Services Provider, taking into account such criteria as the QFC Authority may consider relevant in its absolute discretion, including but not limited to the applicant's:
(1) background and history;
(2) professional memberships;
(3) ownership and Group; and
(4) staffing;
(B) it has adequate professional indemnity insurance which provides cover in respect of work undertaken in the QFC; and
(C) it meets any other requirements prescribed by the QFC Authority.
(4) Where the applicant is established in a jurisdiction other than the QFC, the QFC Authority must be satisfied that:
(A) the applicant is subject in that jurisdiction to licensing and ongoing monitoring of the relevant aspects of its activities;
(B) that the body or bodies that granted the applicant's licence and monitor its activities is or are able to exercise sufficient disciplinary actions over the applicant;
(C) that the applicant has notified its licenser and monitoring body of its intent to register in the QFC; and
(D) that the applicant is in good standing with its licenser and monitoring body.
(5) Where the QFC Authority approves an applicant to appear on the register, the QFC Authority will inform the applicant in writing of the range of services that it is permitted to provide to a Special Company.
(6) If at any time after registration, a Support Services Provider no longer meets the requirements for registration as an approved Support Services Provider, the Support Services Provider must immediately inform the QFC Authority in writing using the form prescribed in Appendix 1.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.5.3 Requirement to file assessment by third party
doc_path: 2.5.3 Requirement to file assessment by third party
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) The QFC Authority may require a Support Services Provider to file with the QFC Authority:
(A) at the time of filing an application for approval and registration; and
(B) at the time of payment of the annual fee or by such later time as the QFC Authority may direct;
an assessment completed within the preceding three months by a firm or body approved for this purpose by the QFC Authority addressing such matters relating to the Support Services Provider as notified by the QFC Authority.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.6.1 Nominee Shareholders
doc_path: 2.6 Application of the QFC Companies Regulations to Special Purpose Companies
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) Article 12.2 of the QFC Special Company Regulations provides that a body corporate incorporated outside the QFC may not be registered as a nominee Shareholder of a Special Purpose Company unless the QFC Authority has confirmed in writing that it does not object to the entity acting as a nominee.
(2) A Special Purpose Company applying for the QFC Authority's non-objection to the appointment of such a body corporate as a nominee Shareholder must:
(A) complete the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority; and
(C) pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
(3) Before the QFC Authority confirms that it does not object to such an appointment, the Special Purpose Company must satisfy the QFC Authority that the proposed nominee:
(A) is fit and proper;
(B) has adequate financial resources;
(C) has adequate internal governance arrangements; and
(D) satisfies such other criteria as the QFC Authority may specify in its absolute discretion.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 2.6.2 Transfers of Shares
doc_path: 2.6 Application of the QFC Companies Regulations to Special Purpose Companies
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) Article 12.3 of the QFC Special Company Regulations provides that a Special Purpose Company may not register a transfer of shares in the Special Purpose Company until the QFC Authority has confirmed in writing that it does not object to such a transfer.
(2) A Special Purpose Company applying for the QFC Authority's non-objection to such a transfer must:
(A) complete the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority including details and any changes to the details of Beneficial Owners of the proposed shareholders; and
(C) pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
(3) Before the QFC Authority confirms that it does not object to such a transfer, the Special Purpose Company must satisfy the QFC Authority that the proposed transferee is fit and proper to be registered as a Shareholder of the Special Purpose Company.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.content_text: When assessing an application to conduct Holding Company Activities, the QFC Authority may consider any of the following criteria, as well as any other criteria which in its sole discretion considers relevant in order to further the QFC Authority's objectives in Article 5 of the QFC Law: (A) the background and history of the applicant; (B) the fitness and propriety of individuals performing the Senior Executive Function; (C) the fitness and propriety of the persons who Control the applicant (for this purpose Control has the meaning set out in the QFCA Rules, Part 2 - General Rules, Rule 8.2.1 ); (D) the ownership of the applicant, including the identity and details of Beneficial Owners of the applicant; (E) whether the proposed business plan of the applicant is likely to be beneficial to the development of the QFC; and (F) such other criteria as the QFC Authority may consider relevant or necessary. QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 3.6 Transfers of Shares
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) Article 23B of the QFC Special Company Regulations provides that a Holding Company may not register a transfer of shares in the Holding Company until the QFC Authority has confirmed in writing that it does not object to such a transfer.
(2) A Holding Company applying for the QFC Authority's non-objection to such a transfer must:
(A) complete the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and file it with the QFC Authority;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the QFC Authority, including details and any changes to the details of the Beneficial Owners of the proposed shareholders; and
(C) pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the QFC Authority.
(3) Before the QFC Authority confirms that it does not object to such a transfer, the Holding Company must satisfy the QFC Authority that the proposed transferee is fit and proper to be registered as a Shareholder of the Holding Company.

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 4.2.5 Revocation of status by the CRO
doc_path: 4. Incorporation and Registration of Special Companies
4.2 Registration by the CRO as a Special Company
4.2.5 Revocation of status by the CRO
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) The CRO may revoke the status of a Special Company:
(A) on the application of the Special Company itself if the condition in 4.2.5 (3) is met; or
(B) on the QFC Authority's own initiative.
(2) The CRO shall revoke the status of a Company as a Special Purpose Company or a Holding Company by amending the public register so as to remove the words "Special Purpose Company Activities" or "Holding Company Activities", as appropriate, from the section indicating the business activities of the Company.
(3) A Special Company may not apply to the CRO for the revocation of its status as a Special Company until it has complied with the relevant requirements of Article 29.2 of the QFC Special Company Regulations and it has been issued with an amended Licence by the QFC Authority and, where applicable, an authorisation by the QFC Regulatory Authority.
(4) A Special Company applying to the CRO for the revocation of its status as a Special Company must:
(A) complete the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and file it with the CRO;
(B) provide such additional material as may be required by the CRO; and
(C) pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the CRO.
(5) The CRO may not revoke the status of a Special Company on the application of the Special Company itself unless it has received written notice from the QFC Authority confirming that the Special Company is no longer performing Special Purpose Company Activities or Holding Company Activities as appropriate.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).

QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.title: 5. Amendment of Articles of Association
QFCA Rules :: Special Company Rules.document_html:
(1) Article 25.5 of the QFC Special Company Regulations provides that a Special Company must give no less than twenty-one days' prior written notice to the CRO of any proposal to amend its Articles of Association and that the CRO may consult with the QFC Authority and Regulatory Authority as appropriate and object to the proposed amendment if it is not in line with the status of a Special Company.
(2) A Special Company must provide notice to the CRO of such proposed amendment using the form prescribed in Appendix 1 and pay the fee prescribed in Appendix 2 to the CRO.
(3) The Special Company's application must include:
(A) a copy of the proposed amended Articles of Association;
(B) a detailed description of the reasons for the proposed amendment;
(C) confirmation that the proposed amended Articles of Association still comply with the requirements of Article 25 of the QFC Special Company Regulations; and
(D) an explanation as to why the proposed amendment is in line with the status of the Company as a Special Company.
(4) The twenty-one day period prescribed in Article 25.5 of the QFC Special Company Regulations will not begin until the Special Company submits an application conforming in all respects to the above criteria.
Amended (as from 19th October 2017).
